pr.title: docs/ gains a CLI manual, and the commands stop living only in --help
pr.head: d0adbc371a66a490e264583edeab507c5bf0edc6

summary: Field is a command-line tool for music production. A Field project is a Git repository of YAML files, and the field command builds its audio through a dependency graph with a content-addressed cache. The docs/ directory explains the concepts (tracks, the project model, the build graph, the audio engine), but no page said what to type. This pull request adds docs/cli.md, a manual organized by task: install, labels, check, look around, build, play, the transport, record, export, sharing through a remote, create, generate, plugins, and sc render, then environment variables, platform notes, and a command table.

The manual's examples are transcripts taken from examples/bloom, the two-song example project in this repository. Most of them use the song tall-grass, because the other song, creek, depends on generated takes that bloom does not commit, so a fresh checkout cannot build it. Two one-line edits list the new page in docs/README.md and in AGENTS.md.

The branch was written in August against an older main. On 2026-10-10, main was merged into it, and the manual was then brought up to date with recording and the remote commands that the merge pulled in. Every finding thread is resolved, the latest review is clean, and a human approval is what remains. The pull request body asks for it to merge after #161, the Windows port, because the platform note cites a plan amendment that #161 carries.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• 2026-08-18. The author's own two passes. The play fallback paragraph was rewritten to describe today's behavior and to name the Windows port, #161, as in flight.
  • 2026-09-07, on dcabd76. A Projector review filed two findings: two plan links that the Projector layout move broke, and two transcripts on creek/track:space that fail on a fresh checkout.
  • 2026-10-10, on 6a310a4. After the merge of main, the link finding was fixed. Three new findings: four transcripts that differed from what the code prints, play refusals that no longer existed, and a command reference without recording or the remote commands.
  • 2026-10-10, on d0adbc3. Three commits fixed all four open findings. The review is clean, with two suggestions about over-broad sentences.

cards.title: Terms this page uses
cards.html:
• Label. The address of something buildable, such as //songs/creek/track:main. The CLI also accepts creek/track:main, and a bare song name such as creek means that song's output track.
  • Live song and built artifact. field play creek plays the song live, evaluated in the engine. field play creek/track:main plays the rendered WAV file from disk.
  • field-audiod. The audio daemon. It plays sound, records takes, and renders every stem a build produces.
  • Gen node and take. A generated sound, such as creek/gen:still-water-keys, and one of its generated variants. A recorded take is the same idea for a performance captured by field record.
  • Remote. An audiofield site that hosts a project's Git repository and the renders its author built, so a fresh clone can fetch them instead of rendering.
  • Bloom. examples/bloom, the example project with the songs creek and tall-grass.

groups.title: The CLI manual
groups.kicker: One new page that walks through each task the field command does, with transcripts from examples/bloom
intro: docs/cli.md is for someone with a checkout who wants to use field. Each section names a task, gives the command, and shows what it prints. A label is the address of something buildable, such as //songs/creek/track:main. The CLI also accepts the shorter creek/track:main, and a bare song name means that song's output track.

The distinction the manual leans on most is in the Play section. Naming a bare song plays it live, evaluated in the engine. Naming an explicit label plays the built artifact, a rendered WAV file, from disk. Every play option works on both, except --watch, which follows a live song only. field-audiod is the daemon that plays, records, and renders audio.

Two sections cover what the merge of main added. "Record a take" walks through recording onto a track that carries a record: entry. "Share a project through a remote" covers login, logout, clone, push, and pull. Each section links to docs/audio-engine.md or docs/remote.md for the depth.

checks.text: The review read this head without running it, because its author has no write access to the repository. Each verified note below was traced in src/cli.ts and the command modules it calls.

files.note: The new manual. Read the Play section, the two new sections on recording and the remote, and the command reference most closely.

checks.text: Suggestion: init, clone, login, logout, sc render, and --version run outside a project, and this page documents clone, which a reader runs before a project exists. "Most commands" would be accurate.

Every stem and every rate conversion renders by spawning field-audiod: the stem and resample rules both call renderInsertChain (src/generators/stem.ts, src/generators/resample.ts). Only artifact playback falls back to afplay (src/cli.ts).
This is the line formatRemoteReport prints for a project with no remote and no stored token (src/commands/version.ts). The report always prints it, between the worker protocol and the daemons.
Suggestion: explain takes one label, and record takes one track, because resolveRecordTarget refuses a pattern. Only build, export, and play take several.
These counts match bloom at this head: creek has 14 track files with 25 inputs, and tall-grass has 6 and 6. Counted by parsing the track YAML under examples/bloom/songs/.

This resolves on a fresh checkout. room receives a cable from drums, which places seven-eight-loop, which renders a SuperCollider program. That program is a content-hashed input, not a graph node, so no takeless gen node is reached. deps lists dependencies first and the label last, which is the order shown.

The explain output matches src/cli.ts for a label whose input is not built: the input reads (not built), so there is no action: line and no output: line. The cable line matches formatCable for one arrival.

This replaces the creek examples that failed on a fresh checkout. field query and field explain on a label that depends on creek's generated takes stop with a message that names the field generate command to run.

The status column matches buildStatus in src/cli.ts: the word padded to six characters, two spaces, then the label and its .field/out path. fetched, the fourth word, is seven characters, so a remote hit sits one column right.

This matches playLiveSession in src/commands/play.ts. A live song with --from and --loop sets a region loop that wraps at the content's extent. An artifact takes the requeue path, which locates to the position on every pass. Both kinds of target send the engine click with sendClick.
field devices prints an output: heading, then an input: list with channel counts only when the machine has inputs (src/cli.ts).

A bare - record: with no takes is a warning, and field check still prints ok. src/model/project.test.ts pins this exact flow: createTrack, then this entry. createTrack also places the new track in main, as the sentence above says.

recordTake loads the song as the bed when nothing is loaded, refuses --until or --count-in without --at, and refuses --loop without --until or on a file bed (src/commands/record.ts). Landing moves the WAV to audio/<track>/ and chooses the new take in takes.yaml (src/commands/land.ts).
exportBaseName drops the songs prefix, and a converted export appends .<rate>-<depth>, which starts its own version family (src/commands/export.ts, pinned by src/commands/export.test.ts).

This paragraph follows docs/remote.md, "Which remote" and "The read-through cache". A live field play <song> evaluates dirty subgraphs in the engine instead of rendering them, so only artifact playback asks the remote.
field import reports the song-relative path audio/<name>/<name>.wav (src/commands/import.ts, pinned by src/model/project.test.ts).

#161 is still open, so "in review" is true today. On this branch, §2.2 of the Windows plan is still an open decision with a recommendation. The amendment this sentence cites arrives with #161, which is why the pull request body asks for #161 to merge first.

Both plan links resolve at this head. Listing the tree shows docs/projects/windows-portability/readme.md and docs/projects/linux-portability/readme.md, and the link text keeps the windows-portability.md form that docs/projects/README.md asks for.
The reference lists every command src/cli.ts registers except git-credential, which is hidden from --help because only Git calls it.
